blocks: Today we gather here in solemn assembly to commemorate the 150th anniversary of the birth of Dr Sun Yat-sen, to honour his immortal contributions to national independence, social progress and the people's happiness, to carry forward his revolutionary spirit and noble character, and to inspire the sons and daughters of the Chinese nation at home and abroad to unite and strive for the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

Dr Sun Yat-sen was a great national hero, a great patriot and a great forerunner of China's democratic revolution. He took revolution as his life's mission, resolved to save the country and the people, and made contributions to the Chinese nation that shine in the annals of history.

The times make great figures, and great figures in turn shape their times. When Dr Sun Yat-sen was born 150 years ago, China was suffering the savage aggression of the imperialist powers and the decadent rule of the feudal autocratic system. Wars were frequent and the people destitute; the Chinese nation had fallen into an abyss of turmoil at home and humiliation from abroad, and the Chinese people lived in misery. In that dark and stormy age the Chinese nation never submitted. Countless people of lofty ideals stepped forward one after another to seek a path to save the country and the people and waged a heroic struggle. Dr Sun Yat-sen was the outstanding representative among them.

As a young man Dr Sun Yat-sen saw the land shattered and the people suffering, and vowed "to rescue the people from fire and flood at once, and to prop up the great edifice before it falls". He raised the banner against feudal autocratic rule and threw himself resolutely into the cause of democratic revolution. He founded the Revive China Society and the Tongmenghui, put forward the Three Principles of the People (nationalism, democracy and the people's livelihood), spread revolutionary ideas actively, united revolutionary forces widely, and launched armed uprisings one after another, travelling everywhere and crying out to advance the democratic revolution.

In 1911, under his leadership and influence, the 1911 Revolution that shook the world succeeded. It overthrew the Qing dynasty and ended the monarchical autocracy that had ruled China for thousands of years. Constrained by the course of history and by social conditions, the 1911 Revolution did not change the semi-colonial, semi-feudal nature of old China, did not change the tragic fate of the Chinese people, and did not complete the historic task of national independence and the people's liberation. But it began a modern national democratic revolution in the full sense, opened the floodgates of progress in China, spread the idea of a democratic republic, greatly advanced the liberation of the Chinese nation's thinking, and with immense force and influence pushed forward China's social transformation.

Dr Sun Yat-sen's greatness lies not only in his leading the 1911 Revolution but also in his keeping pace with the times, refining his revolutionary ideas and strategy of struggle in order to realize his revolutionary ideals, and fighting without compromise against every force that went against the tide of the times. He firmly opposed warlord division and separatism and firmly upheld the democratic republic and the integrity and unity of the country. After the October Revolution broke out and Marxism-Leninism came to China, it opened new horizons for Dr Sun Yat-sen's understanding of the world and of China. After the Communist Party of China was founded, Dr Sun Yat-sen cooperated sincerely with the Chinese Communists. With the help of the CPC he developed the old Three Principles of the People into the new Three Principles of the People, adopted the Three Great Policies of alliance with Russia, cooperation with the Communists and assistance to the peasants and workers, reorganized the Kuomintang of China, helped carry the Northern Expedition to victory, and pushed forward the democratic revolution against imperialism and feudalism. Comrade Mao Zedong named the programme of the Three Principles of the People, the united-front policy and the spirit of arduous struggle together as "the most central, most essential and greatest legacy" Dr Sun Yat-sen "left us", and as "the greatest contribution to the Chinese nation".

Grieved by the poverty and weakness of the China of his day, Dr Sun Yat-sen was the first to sound the resounding call to "rejuvenate China" (振兴中华). He held that "construction is the sole purpose of revolution". He was convinced that after the revolution succeeded, through the efforts of the whole nation, China would certainly catch up with the advanced countries of the world. He said with great passion: "Once the great goal of renewing China is achieved, not only will the dawn of a new era break over our beautiful country, but all of mankind will share a brighter future."

Dr Sun Yat-sen made outstanding contributions to the Chinese people and the Chinese nation. He enjoys high prestige in the hearts of the Chinese people and is revered by all the sons and daughters of the Chinese nation. Today, as we honour the historic achievements Dr Sun Yat-sen made and his glorious life devoted wholly to the Chinese people, our hearts are filled with deep reverence.

Chinese Communists are the most steadfast supporters, the most loyal partners and the most faithful successors of Dr Sun Yat-sen's revolutionary cause. In his lifetime Chinese Communists firmly supported Dr Sun Yat-sen's cause. After his death Chinese Communists faithfully carried on his unfinished mission, united and led the people of all ethnic groups in heroic struggle and continued advance at enormous sacrifice, completed Dr Sun Yat-sen's unfinished cause, won victory in the new-democratic revolution, founded the People's Republic of China in which the people are masters of the country, and achieved national independence and the people's liberation. On that basis Chinese Communists united and led the Chinese people in continued struggle, completed the socialist revolution and established the socialist system.

In the 67 years since the founding of New China, and especially in more than 30 years of reform and opening up, the Chinese people under the leadership of the Communist Party of China have made one great leap after another on the socialist road and achieved great accomplishments that have drawn the world's attention. Today we can tell Dr Sun Yat-sen, by way of comfort, that we are closer than at any time in history to the goal of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and more confident and more capable than at any time in history of reaching it.

The best way for us to commemorate Dr Sun Yat-sen is to learn from and carry on his precious spirit, unite all forces that can be united, mobilize all factors that can be mobilized, and keep striving for the rejuvenation of China that he longed for.

We must learn from Dr Sun Yat-sen's lofty example of loving the motherland and devoting himself to it. Dr Sun Yat-sen's greatest trait was his love of country. All his life he pursued the ideal of national independence, development and rejuvenation, unwavering and utterly firm. Dr Sun Yat-sen said: "What is the greatest thing in being a person? It is to know how to love one's country." He always spurred himself on with sayings such as "love the country as one's life" and "while a breath remains, never forget to save the country". He had a high degree of national self-respect and national self-confidence. He did not cling to the ancient or keep to the old, and did not worship or fawn on the foreign, stressing that "since Chinese society differs from that of Europe and America, the politics that governs society naturally differs from that of Europe and America too", and that "if the power to develop lies in our own hands we survive; if it lies in others' hands we perish". From his rough life experience and long practice of struggle he drew one lesson: to remake China one must start from China's realities and take a path suited to China's national conditions.

History, ancient and modern, Chinese and foreign, tells us that no nation in the world has achieved its own development and rejuvenation by following step by step in the path of others, and that no fixed path can lead every nation to development and rejuvenation; every nation that has developed and revived successfully has found a path suited to its own realities. Today, to open a new chapter in the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, we must vigorously carry forward the great spirit of patriotism and believe firmly that the Chinese nation is capable of taking a successful path to rejuvenation. Patriotism is concrete and real. In contemporary China, to carry forward patriotism one must understand deeply that the leadership of the Communist Party of China and China's socialist system must be upheld for a long time without wavering; that socialism with Chinese characteristics, which the CPC has led the Chinese people in opening up, must be upheld for a long time without wavering; and that the CPC's and the Chinese people's basic policy of rooting themselves in China, drawing on the fine achievements of human civilization, and developing the country independently must be upheld for a long time without wavering. We must strengthen our confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and guard and build our great country well, steadfastly along the road of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

We must learn from Dr Sun Yat-sen's broad-minded devotion to the world belonging to all and to the welfare of the people. Dr Sun Yat-sen had deep feeling for the people. All his life he held "the world belongs to all" (天下为公) as the highest realm of thought and devoted himself to "removing the people's sorrows and seeking happiness for the people", unwavering and utterly firm. Dr Sun Yat-sen knew that the people are the greatest force, and stressed that to achieve the aims of the revolution the masses must be awakened. He cared about the people's hardships and stressed that "the foundation of the state lies in the people", that "the people's livelihood is the centre of gravity of social evolution", and that "what the people cannot do, we must do for them; where the people have no rights, we must fight for them". He earnestly urged everyone "to set your heart on doing great things, not on becoming a great official". His deep feeling for the people was the source of his strength in pursuing truth and committing himself to revolution, and the deep foundation of his unceasing struggle and refusal ever to give up.

For any great cause to succeed it must find its roots among the people, gather its strength from the people, and be accomplished by the people together. Go against the people's will and lose their support, and any cause becomes water without a source or a tree without roots, and cannot succeed. Today, to open a new chapter in the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, our Party must always take serving the people wholeheartedly as its fundamental purpose, always take the people's endorsement and support as its source of strength, and keep the people in the highest place in its heart. We must do everything for the people and rely on the people in everything, always keep a child's devotion to the people, always stand together with the people, see that the fruits of reform and development benefit all the people more and more fairly, keep advancing toward the goal of common prosperity for all, and unite more than 1.3 billion Chinese people into a mighty force driving the development and growth of the Chinese nation.

We must learn from Dr Sun Yat-sen's fine quality of pursuing truth and keeping pace with the times. Dr Sun Yat-sen had a broad outlook and an open mind. All his life he pursued truth and held to it, unwavering and utterly firm. No one in the world is born knowing everything. Dr Sun Yat-sen took as his motto "the tide of the world is vast and mighty; those who follow it prosper, those who resist it perish". He was good at learning from practice, including from the lessons of failure, and so was able "to suit the tide of the world and meet the needs of society". He said: "Apart from revolution, my only passion in life is reading; I cannot live a day without reading." He never stopped exploring and moving forward, and never refused to revise his own thinking and positions. He always examined China's situation within and the tide of the world without, took in the strengths of all and added new creations of his own, and strove to keep up with the tide of the times. Both his transformation from a social reformist into a firm democratic revolutionary and his development of the old Three Principles of the People into the new embody his precious spirit of daring to break through limits and constantly renew himself.

The wheel of history rolls forward, and those who cannot keep up will fall behind and be eliminated by history. History favours only the steadfast, the striving and the combative; it does not wait for the hesitant, the slack or those who shrink from difficulty. Today, to open a new chapter in the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, we must take a grand historical view, grasp the overall trend of world development, listen to the voice of the times, have the courage to uphold truth and correct mistakes, and keep advancing innovation in theory, practice, institutions, culture and every other field, writing a new chapter in the Chinese nation's development in the onward torrent of the times.

We must learn from Dr Sun Yat-sen's spirit of tenacious and indomitable struggle. Dr Sun Yat-sen "devoted himself to the national revolution for forty years", and all his life he held that "where my will is set I go forward without retreat; the more I am thwarted the harder I strive, and I try again and again", unwavering and utterly firm. Dr Sun Yat-sen said: "To lay with our mortal lives of a few decades the immortal foundation of a state for ten thousand years: its worth can be known." His revolutionary career met setback after setback and every hardship, but to "create an independent and free country that upholds the interests of the state and the people" he never lost heart because of failure and never retreated before difficulty. He believed that "if my heart believes a thing can be done, then even a task as hard as moving mountains and filling seas will one day succeed; if my heart believes it cannot be done, then even a task as easy as turning one's hand or snapping a twig will never bear fruit", and that so long as one "concentrates the spirit and presses forward with full force, in keeping with the tide of the world's progress and with the natural law by which good grows and evil wanes, there will in the end be a day of final success". No external threat, internal division or temporary defeat could shake his revolutionary will. Even on his deathbed what he never forgot was "peace, struggle, save China". Dr Sun Yat-sen fulfilled his vow with a lifetime of struggle and showed the heroism and dedication of a great revolutionary.

A great cause is great not only because it is just and grand, but also because it never runs smoothly. A great figure is great not only because he has made great contributions to the people, the nation and mankind, but also because he forged a strong will and noble character through hard trials. Today, to open a new chapter in the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, we must soberly assess the profound and complex changes in the international situation, grasp fully the arduous tasks of reform, development and stability, and make long and unremitting efforts; we must never imagine at any time that we can reach our goals easily, with drums beating and gongs clanging. We must shoulder our responsibilities and be ready at all times to meet major challenges, resist major risks, overcome major obstacles and resolve major contradictions, and with the courage to brave dangers and tackle difficulties and the drive to forge ahead, keep advancing the cause of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

Dr Sun Yat-sen always firmly upheld national unity and ethnic solidarity, and clearly opposed all words and deeds that would split the country or divide the nation. Dr Sun Yat-sen said: "China is a unified country; this is firmly imprinted in our country's historical consciousness, and it is this consciousness that has allowed us to be preserved as a country." He stressed: "'Unification' is the hope of all the citizens of China. If we can unify, the whole people will enjoy happiness; if we cannot, they will suffer."

Achieving the complete reunification of the motherland is where the fundamental interests of the Chinese nation lie, and the shared aspiration and sacred duty of all the sons and daughters of the Chinese nation. Ensuring that the country remains whole and is not split, and safeguarding the fundamental interests of the Chinese nation, is the common will of all the sons and daughters of the Chinese nation and an unstoppable historical trend.

Compatriots on both sides of the Strait are flesh-and-blood brothers bound by blood. The two sides of the Strait are an inseparable community of shared destiny. The peaceful development of cross-Strait relations is the right path to maintaining peace across the Strait, promoting common development and benefiting compatriots on both sides. We adhere to the common political foundation of the "1992 Consensus", deepen cross-Strait economic and social integration, and enhance our compatriots' well-being and kinship. Any party, group or individual in Taiwan, whatever it advocated in the past, provided it recognizes the "1992 Consensus" and accepts that the mainland and Taiwan belong to one and the same China, we are willing to deal with.

The future and destiny of compatriots on both sides of the Strait are inseparable from the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Compatriots on both sides of the Strait and all the sons and daughters of the Chinese nation at home and abroad must join hands to oppose "Taiwan independence" separatist forces together, to work together for the peaceful development of cross-Strait relations and the complete reunification of the motherland, and to create together a happy life and a bright future for all Chinese.

Since modern times China has endured more than a century of tragic history in which the country was broken and our compatriots trampled, and every son and daughter of the Chinese nation remembers it to the bone. Safeguarding national sovereignty and territorial integrity, and never tolerating a repetition of the historical tragedy of national division, is our solemn commitment to history and to the people. All activities to split the country will be resolutely opposed by the whole Chinese people. We will never allow any person, any organization or any political party, at any time or in any form, to separate any part of Chinese territory from China!

When the country and the nation do well, everyone does well. Dr Sun Yat-sen's lifelong struggle was to see China become "the richest and strongest country in the world" and "the most peaceful and contented country in the world", and the Chinese people "the happiest people in the world". Dr Sun Yat-sen hoped "to carry forward our inherent culture and also absorb the culture of the world and make it shine, so as to stand abreast with all nations in the world".

Throughout his intense revolutionary activity Dr Sun Yat-sen kept thinking about the question of building China. From 1917 to 1919 he wrote The Fundamentals of National Reconstruction (《建国方略》), setting out a grand blueprint for China's construction. It proposed building about 160,000 kilometres of railway to link China's coast, interior and frontiers; building 1.6 million kilometres of highway to form a road network across the country and reaching onto the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau; cutting and dredging the country's waterways and canals, building a Three Gorges dam, and developing inland navigation, water conservancy and electric power; building a world-class seaport on each of China's northern, central and southern coasts; and vigorously developing agriculture, manufacturing and mining. The blueprint Dr Sun Yat-sen drew showed his outstanding insight into and strong hopes for China's development. At the time some foreign journalists thought these ideas pure fantasy, impossible to realize.

Indeed, under the political, economic and social conditions of old China these grand visions could hardly be realized. Today, under the leadership of the Communist Party of China and through the tenacious struggle of the people of all our ethnic groups, the blueprint Dr Sun Yat-sen drew has long since been realized, and many of the Chinese people's achievements go far beyond what he envisioned. Across the land of the motherland, railways reach Qinghai and Tibet, highways form a dense network, a calm lake rises in the high gorges, ports connect to the five oceans, industries span every category, rice and wheat are fragrant everywhere, Shenzhou spacecraft roam space, and national defence is stronger. The independent, democratic, prosperous and strong country Dr Sun Yat-sen strove to build has long stood tall in the East.

Practice fully shows that so long as our path, theory, system and culture are right, so long as we are steadfast, tenacious, persistent and hard-working, and press on toward our great goal with perseverance, unshaken by wind and rain, our goals can be reached, and they certainly will be reached!

Ninety-two years ago Dr Sun Yat-sen expressed his hope for the Chinese nation this way: "If China grows strong, we must not only restore the nation's standing but also bear a great responsibility toward the world." Sixty years ago, commemorating the 90th anniversary of Dr Sun Yat-sen's birth, Comrade Mao Zedong said: "China ought to make a greater contribution to humanity." Thirty years ago Comrade Deng Xiaoping said: "The country's overall strength will be greater, and it can do more for humanity and contribute more to solving the North-South problem. That is the great ambition we have." The Chinese people hope not only to develop well themselves but also that all countries develop well, and that the people of every country can enjoy happy and peaceful lives. We must promote a new type of international relations with win-win cooperation at its core, promote the formation of a community with a shared future and a community of shared interests for mankind, and always be a builder of world peace, a contributor to global development and a defender of the international order, creating together with the people of all countries a bright future of peace and development for humanity.

Over more than 5,000 years the Chinese nation has already made great contributions to humanity in the course of its own development. In the years to come the Chinese people and the Chinese nation will surely keep making new and greater contributions to the noble cause of peace and development for humanity!

Dr Sun Yat-sen said in his day: "With a population of four hundred million and the riches of land stretching tens of thousands of li, we can rouse ourselves to become strong and be invincible under heaven." "I only hope that you, gentlemen, will place the responsibility for rejuvenating China upon your own shoulders." In the last moments of his life Dr Sun Yat-sen still enjoined that the revolution had not yet succeeded and that comrades must still strive. To achieve China's modernization, the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and common prosperity for all the Chinese people, we still have a long way to go and many difficulties and risks to overcome.

I call on all the sons and daughters of the Chinese nation who revere Dr Sun Yat-sen, including compatriots on the mainland, in Hong Kong and Macao, in Taiwan and overseas, whatever their party or belief and wherever they are, to unite more closely, seize the historic opportunity and shoulder the historic responsibility, and carry forward the great cause for which Dr Sun Yat-sen and all the revolutionary forerunners strove! Carry forward the great cause for which all people of lofty ideals since modern times have strived! Carry forward the great cause for which the Chinese people and the Chinese nation have striven since modern times!
